INTEGRATED SCIENCE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #3
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Integrated Science? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Integrated Science.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Integrated Science.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Integrated Science.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Integrated Science.

2. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Milk souring
   D. Iron rusting

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Laboratory Safety? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Laboratory Safety.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Laboratory Safety.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Laboratory Safety.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Laboratory Safety.

4. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 37 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 0 °C

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Magnetism? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Magnetism.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Magnetism.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Magnetism.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Magnetism.

6. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Human Excretory System 18 4.0 Force and Energy 4.1 Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magn? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Human Excretory System 18 4.0 Force and Energy 4.1 Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magn.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Human Excretory System 18 4.0 Force and Energy 4.1 Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magn.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Human Excretory System 18 4.0 Force and Energy 4.1 Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magn.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Human Excretory System 18 4.0 Force and Energy 4.1 Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magn.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Laboratory apparatus and instruments? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Laboratory apparatus and instruments.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Laboratory apparatus and instruments.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Laboratory apparatus and instruments.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Laboratory apparatus and instruments.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Human Excretory System? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Human Excretory System.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Human Excretory System.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Human Excretory System.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Human Excretory System.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Mixtures? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Mixtures.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Mixtures.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Mixtures.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Mixtures.

11. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

12. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Acids, Bases and Indicators? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Acids, Bases and Indicators.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Acids, Bases and Indicators.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Acids, Bases and Indicators.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Acids, Bases and Indicators.

14. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Only carbon dioxide

15. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Human Reproductive System? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Human Reproductive System.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Human Reproductive System.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Human Reproductive System.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Human Reproductive System.

17. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. watt (W)
   C. newton (N)
   D. joule (J)

18. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Electrical Energy? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Electrical Energy.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Electrical Energy.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Electrical Energy.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Electrical Energy.

19. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magnetism 16 Total Number of Lessons 150 Note: The sugg? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magnetism 16 Total Number of Lessons 150 Note: The sugg.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magnetism 16 Total Number of Lessons 150 Note: The sugg.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magnetism 16 Total Number of Lessons 150 Note: The sugg.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magnetism 16 Total Number of Lessons 150 Note: The sugg.

20. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

21. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Primary consumers only

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
22. In three clear sentences, explain Laboratory Safety and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Laboratory apparatus and instruments and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Mixtures and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

28. In three clear sentences, explain Human Excretory System and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

29. In three clear sentences, explain Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magnetism 16 Total Number of Lessons 150 Note: The sugg and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

30. In three clear sentences, explain Electrical Energy and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

31. In three clear sentences, explain Magnetism and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
